questions.question: During a trip, which shut-off valves should be open?

options.text: All shut-off valves should be open.
The rear shut-off valves should be open.
Open all shut-off valves except the rear ones.
No shut-off valves should be open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open all shut-off valves except the rear ones.
questions.explanation: Before starting a trip, open all shut-off valves except the last ones on the rear trailer. Air must reach the brakes on all trailers. Air should not escape from the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: If you don't keep the fifth wheel plate greased, what could happen?
questions.explanation: If the fifth wheel plate is not greased, friction builds up between the tractor and trailer. This causes steering problems.

questions.question: When inspecting a coupling, you should go under the trailer and:

options.text: Detach the jaws from the kingpin.
Put the locking lever in the "emergency" position.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling, go under the trailer and look into the back of the fifth wheel. Check that the jaws are locked tightly around the kingpin.

questions.question: Pull out the trailer air supply control to test:
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before starting a trip. After making sure the trailer rolls freely, pull out the trailer air supply control to test the emergency brakes. Pull forward slowly. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: When coupling glad hands, match the colors. Service lines are often what color?
questions.explanation: When coupling glad hands, match the colors of the glad hands together. Service lines are usually blue. Emergency lines are usually red. This color coding helps drivers avoid mistakes.

questions.question: Trailers made after what year must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?
questions.explanation: Trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: The emergency air line:

options.text: Is controlled by the foot brake.
Is connected to the relay valves.
Supplies air to the trailer air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supplies air to the trailer air tanks.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) does two things. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks on a combination vehicle. It also controls the emergency brakes.

questions.question: The best way to know your trailer is skidding is by:
questions.explanation: The best and earliest way to spot a trailer skid is to see the trailer moving off-course in your mirrors.

questions.question: What causes more than half of all accident-related truck driver deaths?
questions.explanation: Truck rollovers cause more than half of all accident-related truck driver deaths. To prevent rollovers, load cargo low and centered on your truck. Take corners slowly.

questions.question: If your vehicle was built before 1998 and you're not sure if the trailer has Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS), you can:

options.text: Check for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.
Look for a red light on the front right corner of the converter dolly.
Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle was built before 1998 and you're unsure if the trailer has ABS, check under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.

questions.question: What happens when an air supply control is set to "emergency"?
questions.explanation: When an air supply control is set to "emergency," it stops the air supply and applies the trailer emergency brakes.

questions.question: How should you brake in a tractor-trailer with ABS?

options.text: Use extra force to make ABS activate.
Brake the way you normally would.
Use less braking pressure than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the way you normally would.
questions.explanation: Brake in an ABS-equipped truck the same way you would in any other vehicle.

questions.question: Where should the heaviest trailer be positioned in a double or triple combination?

options.text: The weight must be split evenly between all trailers.

questions.explanation: Place the heaviest trailer closest to the tractor. The lightest trailer should be at the rear.

questions.question: What is a bobtail?

options.text: A tractor that drives faster than the speed limit.
A tractor that drives slower than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: A bobtail is a tractor without any trailer attached.

questions.question: What should you know about driving a bobtail tractor?

options.text: Bobtails cannot go as fast as tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
questions.explanation: Bobtails take longer to stop than tractors with loaded trailers. Be prepared for longer stopping distances.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors near the brakes.
Drive on a slippery surface to see if ABS activates.
Remove a tire and check the axle for an ABS sensor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors near the brakes.
questions.explanation: Check under the trailer for wheel speed sensor wires coming from the back of the brakes to determine if it has ABS.

questions.question: How do you prevent a trailer from rolling over?

options.text: Speed up when approaching a corner.
Take on-ramps faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.explanation: To prevent rollovers, keep cargo weight low and drive slowly around turns.

questions.question: What color is used for service lines on glad hands?
questions.explanation: Service lines are blue. Emergency lines are red.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The service line is also called the control line or signal line.

questions.question: What can the "crack-the-whip" effect do?
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect can cause a trailer to turn over during a lane change. Avoid this by making lane changes slowly and safely.
